Bug_Details:
Use StringBuffer.length() to determine StringBuffer length rather than using StringBuffer.toString().equals("")
or StringBuffer.toString().length() == ...
Examples:
StringBuffer sb = new StringBuffer();

if (sb.toString().equals("")) {}        // inefficient

if (sb.length() == 0) {}                // preferred
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by using sb.toString().equals("") to check if the StringBuffer is empty, which is inefficient compared to using sb.length() == 0.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method with both an empty and non-empty StringBuffer. The method uses sb.toString().equals(""), which is inefficient and triggers the bug.
